text: That is the Smithsonian Nature History Museum.  The Smithsonian Museum is a collection of 21 museums.  The Smithsonian Air and Space Museum was my favorite. Arlington National Cemetery is a must stop in while in DC.  You will see how many men and women that gave their lives for our freedom. You can actually look me up at the Women's Military Memorial or Women in Military Service For America Memorial located at Arlington. I love my country so much, seeing it's history up close is an incredible experience. At least it was for me.  Thanks for taking us with you today.

Ryan, you did great, but honestly, Niagara Falls is something you HAVE to experience when it’s warm outside 😭  
Your boat tours weren’t even running, and those boats are literally the best part because that’s where you actually get the iconic view from the American side.

And the best part is going in warm weather — when it’s hot outside and the mist from the falls feels insanely refreshing. That feeling is unmatched.

video_title: I Survived 50 Hours in Meta Glasses
author: @semisemicoloncolon
text:
I really appreciate how Ryan doesn’t just blindly praise and hype up products such as this one, like a lot of other YouTubers would. He’s instead really transparent in his coverage of them and doesn’t shy away from the ways it falls short. It has a really optimistic message, to me, about the importance of humanity and detaching from this technology that, though fancy, won’t replace the authentic human experience, and it’s incredibly refreshing amidst the storm of hyper-tech focused media with depressing implications that we find ourselves in. 
It’s this kind of genuineness that keeps me coming back to Ryan’s content, though I’m probably older than most of his audience. He is more concerned with doing good than retaining viewership and making money, and I wish I could say the same about more content creators, especially those geared towards younger audiences. He kinda feels like a modern Mr. Rogers in that sense; just a genuine kind soul.

text: 11:03 Hello Ryan! The reason the Golden Gate Bridge has the word “golden” in its name is not because the bridge is gold-colored, but because it spans the Golden Gate Strait, the narrow waterway connecting the Pacific Ocean to San Francisco Bay. The strait was named “Golden Gate” in 1846 by explorer John C. Frémont, who believed it would become a valuable gateway for trade and opportunity, much like a “golden gate” to the Pacific. When the bridge was built decades later, it simply took the name of the strait it crossed. In fact, the bridge is painted a distinctive reddish-orange color called International Orange, which was chosen because it stands out well against the region’s frequent fog. So, even though the bridge is not actually golden, its name comes from the historic waterway beneath it rather than its appearance.

author: @Lexithepoptart
text: A friend sent me this, saying “BURNSVILLE CENTER MENTIONED” but she didn’t tell me anything else. This actually made me really emotional. My friends and I used to go to their Spirit Halloween every November and we would read creepypastas in the abandoned minigolf/bumper cart area. There was a model train store that I loved to stare at. One of the employees at the Colombian place in the food court (has since shut down) told me I have the most beautiful eyes and I still think about her. Burnsville Center is less than fifteen minutes away from the Mall of America, which is likely why there are so few shoppers. But it was the closest mall to my friend’s apartment and we loved it there.
